title: Cohen-Macaulayness at a point is equivalent to the existence of a flat quasi-finite map to affine space
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a flat locally finitely presented morphism at a point of fibre dimension d, the lemma shows that Cohen-Macaulayness there is equivalent to the existence of a locally quasi-finite map from a neighbourhood to affine d-space over the base that is flat at the point, and also to the statement that every quasi-finite map from a neighbourhood to affine d-space is automatically flat there. The proof constructs such a map from a system of parameters of the fibre and then reads Cohen-Macaulayness off the resulting flatness, using the dimension d as the number of parameters. Constructing the map from parameters and extracting the equivalence is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 6032-6065.
